meta.purpose: Every number used in the valuation and projection work, separated into (a) verified official figures and (b) labelled analyst assumptions that the client can change.
meta.hard_rule: No verified figure is ever estimated. No assumption is ever presented as data.
meta.update_note: Verified inputs re-read from the official sources on 2026-11-07. The 10-year Treasury moved from 4.90% (2026-11-04) to 4.84% (2026-11-05); Los Angeles CPI from 3.6% (Aug 2026) to 3.7% (Sep 2026); metro job growth from +0.6% (Aug) to +0.5% (Sep). Assumptions A12-A16 were added so the workbook can test more than one lease-rent level and can size a lender-format debt service.

analyst_assumptions.label: Subject base rent used in the model
analyst_assumptions.basis: 8.0% of the verified FY2025 franchise AUV ($1,874k). This is a benchmark, NOT the subject's actual rent. Replace with the leases's contract rent (P03).

analyst_assumptions.label: Contract rent escalation
analyst_assumptions.basis: Typical NNN escalation band of 1.5%-3.0%. Observed metro CPI is 3.7% (verified, S1, Sep 2026), so a 2.0% escalator transfers real value to the landlord only if the lease compounds it.

analyst_assumptions.label: Lease expiration date used
analyst_assumptions.basis: Midpoint of the stated 2030-2035 window. Actual date is P02 and is material: each year shifts NPV.

analyst_assumptions.label: Discount rate for owner-level cash flows
analyst_assumptions.basis: 10-year Treasury 4.84% (verified) plus a 3.16 point illiquidity/single-tenant premium. Premium size is judgment.

analyst_assumptions.label: Exit cap rate - base case
analyst_assumptions.basis: Set inside the 5.50%-7.50% range tested. Anchored directionally to the 7.3% net-lease acquisition yield (verified, S10) which covers all property types and Europe; a single QSR in Los Angeles typically prices tighter. Asset-level cap rate is unverified (M51) and this assumption is the single largest driver of the sell-now price.

analyst_assumptions.label: Brokerage and closing costs on sale
analyst_assumptions.basis: 3.0% brokerage plus 0.5% escrow/title/legal. Negotiable; not a government-published figure.

analyst_assumptions.label: Renewal probability at expiry - base case
analyst_assumptions.basis: Tenant's own filing states it has generally been able to renew at then-current market rates (verified S9). Probability is judgment and scenario-specific.

analyst_assumptions.label: Downtime if the tenant does not renew
analyst_assumptions.basis: Re-tenanting a drive-thru requires entitlement and build-out; no official dataset measures this.

analyst_assumptions.label: Landlord leasing costs on re-tenanting
analyst_assumptions.basis: Tenant improvements plus leasing commission plus carrying costs during downtime. Judgment.

analyst_assumptions.label: Reinvestment yield if sold
analyst_assumptions.basis: Verified 10-year Treasury 4.84% (S11, observation 2026-11-05) as the risk-free alternative. A like-kind exchange into another net-lease asset could plausibly earn 7.0%-7.3% (S10) with added concentration risk.

analyst_assumptions.label: Hold period for the reinvestment comparison
analyst_assumptions.basis: Long enough to span a full cycle after the 2030-2035 expiry.

analyst_assumptions.label: Sensitivity: documented NNN market rent for a modern 1,372 sq ft QSR pad with drive-thru
analyst_assumptions.basis: Sensitivity input, not a data point. Between 9% and 11% of the verified FY2025 franchise AUV ($1,874k, S9), which brackets a typical QSR occupancy-cost ratio. Retail rent is from $10 to $25 per sq ft in the 1,372 sq ft prototype, i.e. roughly $14,000 to $34,000; that is a market convention with no official source, so it is filed as an assumption and not as data.

analyst_assumptions.label: Sensitivity: upper NNN market rent
analyst_assumptions.basis: Sensitivity input, not a data point. Should be read as a 10-year hold with 10% annual NOI growth: at a 6.50% cap the implied value crosses the $5,400,000 Measure ULA tier-1 threshold (S8).

analyst_assumptions.label: All-in NOI as a share of base rent (NNN)
analyst_assumptions.basis: Assumption. In a triple-net lease the tenant reimburses taxes, insurance and CAM, so the landlord's deduction is a credit-loss / vacancy allowance plus a structural reserve. 70% is deliberately conservative. Applied before any debt service.

analyst_assumptions.label: Debt service constant on new acquisition financing
analyst_assumptions.basis: Computed from the verified net-lease acquisition benchmark yield of 7.3% (S10) as an interest rate, 25-year amortization, monthly payments. It is a formula applied to a verified input, not a quoted lender rate. Actual lender terms are unknown (P06).

analyst_assumptions.label: Loan-to-value on new acquisition financing
analyst_assumptions.basis: Assumption. Typical commercial LTV in the current rate environment; lender terms are unknown (P06).

tax_layer.reason: Federal long-term capital gains, unrecaptured Section 1250 depreciation recapture, net investment income tax, and California income tax each depend on the owner's basis, holding period, depreciation history, entity structure, and other income. None of those are in the brief (P05). Publishing a rate stack without them would be a fabrication.
tax_layer.verified_mechanism: Section 1031 permits deferral of gain on the exchange of real property held for productive use or investment, with carryover basis and qualified-intermediary mechanics (S16).
tax_layer.practical_effect: A 1031 exchange is the main tool that separates 'sell' from 'lose 30%+ of the gain'. It is why the recommendation is structured as a sequencing decision, not a binary sell/hold.
